title: How Salary Sacrifice Companies Influence Your Hourly to Annual Pay Estimate
description: Understand how salary sacrifice companies can affect your take-home pay when converting hourly rates to annual salary. Learn about the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual lo
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax deducted according to 2026–27 brackets.

faqs.q: What are salary sacrifice companies and how do they affect my pay calculation?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice companies offer arrangements where you forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This reduces your taxable income but is not accounted for in our simple hourly-to-annual calculator. If you use salary packaging, your actual take-home pay may differ from the estimate because the calculator assumes no salary sacrifice. Check with your employer or a tax professional for personalised advice.

faqs.q: How does casual loading work when converting hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. Our calculator has a checkbox to add this loading automatically. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator will apply it correctly. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25%). When converting to annual, the loading is included in the hourly figure used in the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52.

faqs.q: What tax brackets apply for 2026-27 when estimating annual pay?
faqs.a: For the 2026-27 financial year, the resident tax rates are: nil on income up to $18,200; 15% from $18,201 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $135,000; 37% from $135,001 to $190,000; and 45% above $190,000. A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. Our calculator uses these brackets and the full tax-free threshold. Note that salary sacrifice companies can reduce your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax bracket, but this is not included in the estimate.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have been offered a salary, understanding the full-year picture helps you compare jobs and plan your budget. The standard formula is straightforward: **annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For most full-time employees, the benchmark is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. If you work a different pattern, simply adjust the hours figure. The calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your own hours and includes a checkbox for casual loading.

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate your fortnightly pay by dividing the annual amount by 26 (or multiplying your weekly pay by 2). For example, if your weekly pay is $1,000, your fortnightly pay is $2,000 before tax and super. This can be useful for budgeting if you are paid fortnightly.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for a 38-hour week. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, bringing the minimum to **$33.05 per hour**. However, many employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Award rates vary by industry and role, and they often include penalty rates for weekends, nights, or public holidays. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides more detail on the current rates.

It is important to note that the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of **$2,083.70 per week**. This is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. Your own rate may be higher or lower depending on your award, experience, and location. For job-specific pay data, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) on this site.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave or sick leave. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add casual loading automatically. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator will apply the 25% on top of the base rate you type. For example, if the base rate is $30.00, checking the casual loading box will use $37.50 per hour in the annual calculation. More information is available on the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Superannuation and Salary Sacrifice

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer must pay into a super fund on your behalf. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, paid on top of your salary. This means if your annual gross pay is $80,000, your employer adds $9,600 to your super account, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator estimates super based on ordinary earnings only, and it does not deduct salary sacrifice amounts.

**Salary sacrifice companies** offer arrangements where you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as a car, laptop, or additional super contributions. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower the tax you pay. However, salary sacrifice is not accounted for in our simple hourly-to-annual calculation. If you work for a salary sacrifice company, your actual take-home pay may differ from the estimate because the calculator assumes no salary packaging. For more details, see the [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Once you have your annual gross pay (including casual loading if applicable), you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% generally applies, though low-income earners may be exempt or pay a reduced rate. The calculator uses the full tax-free threshold and the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare (as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide). It does not deduct HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more detailed breakdown of your net pay, visit the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

The easiest way to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures is to use [the timesheet](/) on our home page. Enter your base hourly rate, select whether you are casual (to add 25% loading), and the calculator will show your annual gross pay, super estimate, and approximate tax. You can also adjust the hours per week if you work less or more than 38 hours. Remember that the result is an estimate and does not include salary sacrifice, penalty rates, or allowances.

## Understanding Averages and Your Pay

The ABS Average Weekly Earnings figure of $2,083.70 per week for full-time adults is a useful benchmark, but it is an average across all jobs and industries. It is not a median for your specific occupation. If you are comparing a job offer, check the relevant award or agreement for your role. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context on how averages are calculated and what they mean for your situation.

In summary, converting your hourly rate to annual pay is simple: multiply by hours per week and 52. Add casual loading if applicable, remember that super is paid on top, and use the tax brackets to estimate your take-home pay. If your employer is one of the many **salary sacrifice companies**, your actual tax may be lower, but this calculator does not account for that. Always consult a tax professional for personalised advice.
